content.value_statement: Quantum simulations require precise state, solver, and visualization choices. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through QuTiP workflows for closed and open systems.
actual_capabilities: Creates QuTiP states, density matrices, operators, tensor products, and composite systems.
Selects solvers for Schrodinger, master equation, Monte Carlo, Floquet, and HEOM workflows.
Models open-system dissipation with collapse operators, baths, and stochastic trajectories.
Computes expectation values, entropy, fidelity, concurrence, correlation functions, and steady states.
Builds Bloch sphere, Wigner, Q-function, Fock distribution, Hinton, and matrix histogram visualizations.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for memory use, convergence, tolerances, and solver performance.
limitations: Requires the user environment to have QuTiP and optional packages installed.
Does not validate physical correctness of every model assumption.
Large Hilbert spaces can exceed available memory or runtime.
Examples may need adaptation for the installed QuTiP version.

use_cases.title: Model Open Quantum Systems
use_cases.description: Build Hamiltonians, collapse operators, and solver settings for dissipative dynamics.

use_cases.title: Teach Quantum State Concepts
use_cases.description: Create examples for kets, density matrices, tensor products, Bloch vectors, and measurements.

use_cases.title: Prototype Quantum Algorithms
use_cases.description: Explore gates, entanglement, noise channels, and visualization before moving to production tools.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic State
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this qutip skill to create a two-level quantum state, define Pauli operators, and explain each object in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Simulate Open Dynamics
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me model a damped harmonic oscillator in QuTiP. Choose the solver, define collapse operators, and describe expected observables.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Entanglement
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a QuTiP workflow for two-qubit dephasing. Track concurrence, fidelity, and relevant expectation values over time.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Non-Markovian Study
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a QuTiP HEOM or Bloch-Redfield simulation for a driven system. Include assumptions, convergence checks, and visualization outputs.

output_examples.input: Create a quick QuTiP plan for a damped oscillator.
output: Use a truncated Fock space sized for the expected photon range.
Use a master equation solver with a cavity decay collapse operator.
Track photon number and plot its decay over the chosen time grid.

output_examples.input: I need a phase-space visualization for a coherent state.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Wigner and Q-function plots, explains their interpretation, and suggests axes, colormaps, and resolution choices.

output_examples.input: Compare solvers for a noisy two-qubit model.
output_examples.output: The skill distinguishes unitary, master equation, Monte Carlo, and Bloch-Redfield approaches based on state type and bath assumptions.

best_practices: State the physical system, Hilbert space size, initial state, Hamiltonian, and observables before asking for code.
Ask for convergence checks when using stochastic solvers, truncated spaces, or non-Markovian methods.
Request plots and interpretation together so numerical outputs connect to physical meaning.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for large simulations without dimension limits or performance constraints.
Do not treat example parameters as validated experimental values.
Do not use solver names interchangeably without describing dissipation and state type.

faq.question: What is QuTiP used for?
faq.answer: QuTiP is used to simulate quantum states, operators, dynamics, measurements, and open quantum systems in Python.

faq.question: Does this skill install QuTiP for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and may suggest manual install commands, but installation depends on your environment.

faq.question: Can it handle open quantum systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers collapse operators, master equations, Monte Carlo trajectories, HEOM, and Bloch-Redfield methods.

faq.question: Can it create visualizations?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Bloch spheres, Wigner functions, Q-functions, Fock distributions, Hinton diagrams, and matrix histograms.

faq.question: Does it replace a physics review?
faq.answer: No. You should review assumptions, units, convergence, and model validity for your research or product context.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
